1.0 broke making the cursor not blinking in Vim mode; a CSS snippet that used to fix this stopped working.
Obsidian is less strict than Logseq and allows me to follow whatever principle I want, mixing Zettelkasten, daily notes, and folder structures.
With Obsidian I know that a note is a file. Less convenient but simple and reliable, unlike Logseq's more interconnected but complex system.
Complaint: Obsidian insists on storing images in a single folder by default, which doesn't scale or make it easy to manage complex notes as a single unit.
My only missing feature is better PDF support, similar to Logseq, which lets you embed and annotate PDFs with markdown, area highlights, and math notation.
The new Bases feature is essentially a 90% replacement for the Dataview plugin - not as comprehensive yet, but a lot faster and more responsive.
Using Bases (in beta) for a vault of D&D campaign notes made it much easier to get an overview of NPCs and relevant info; the dev team has been very responsive to beta feedback.
The fact there is no app to do 'RAG on localhost for my own notes' really makes me wonder whether the tech works at all.
The Git plugin is great for single-device backup, but not great for device sync or collaboration - built a real-time collaboration plugin (Relay) using CRDTs to address this.
Confirmed: there is no sandboxing at all - every Obsidian plugin has full access to your computer's filesystem and can make HTTP requests.
Obsidian not being open source makes it harder to verify their security model, unlike other note-taking systems where all code is visible.

Useful plugin list: Ink for drawing (a big miss in the standard feature set), Self-Hosted LiveSync for syncing without third parties, Copilot for local AI via Ollama, Whisper for local dictation, and ReadItLater for web clipping.
This looks like Obsidian's first move away from markdown - Canvas files are JSON, not as readable; hope this isn't a trend toward proprietary formats.
One thing missing from Obsidian is a Google Keep-like view for quickly jotting small notes and seeing recent ones, especially on mobile.
I cannot create a desktop shortcut to open a specific Obsidian vault directly since a vault is a folder, not a recognizable file; also the standard F2 rename shortcut doesn't work, adding friction.
Adding large features like Canvas raises concern - worried about feature bloat like what killed Evernote, which 'did too much, not too little.'
Used Obsidian for running tabletop RPG sessions with folders of monsters, encounters, and player backstory; also replaced Sublime+directory for daily dev note-taking.
I dislike Obsidian's aesthetics and wouldn't use it because of Electron - spoiled by native note apps like Bear and NotePlan on macOS with nicer UX.
Found the graph view quite gimmicky for my workflow, but the rest of Obsidian's features are super polished.
Migrated from Roam to Obsidian and it's really awesome - I have ownership of my files, constant updates with new features and bug fixes, and a really nice community.
